key_insight: A frozen CT-CLIP foundation model with a lightweight survival head can predict lung cancer survival from pretreatment CT plus clinical data, often matching or outperforming other multimodal approaches.
clinical_relevance: This suggests domain-specific pretrained imaging models may help stratify lung cancer patients into clinically meaningful risk groups when labeled survival data are limited.
method: 242 lung cancer patients with pretreatment CT and clinical variables
Compared frozen encoders, full fine-tuning, and low-rank adaptation
Tested modality ablations and clinical/multimodal baselines
evidence_signal: In this cohort evaluation, the frozen CT-CLIP setup with a trainable survival head outperformed the clinical-only baseline and achieved comparable or improved performance versus other multimodal methods.
watch_item: The findings come from a relatively small retrospective cohort, so external validation and careful implementation are needed before clinical use.
paper_title: CT-CLIP Representations for Multimodal Lung Cancer Survival Prediction
